q: The Jordan normal form theorem states that every matrix A over ℂ is similar to a block diagonal matrix with Jordan blocks. A Jordan block J_k(λ) is a k×k matrix with λ on the diagonal and:
opts: 1 on the superdiagonal and 0 elsewhere off diagonal
exp: A Jordan block J_k(λ) has λ on the diagonal, 1 on the superdiagonal, 0 elsewhere. The number and sizes of Jordan blocks for each eigenvalue λ are uniquely determined by the dimensions of ker(A−λI)^k (the invariant factor structure).
